newsitem.title: CHILE: Ruling coalition winning Chilean local elections.
newsitem.headline: Ruling coalition winning Chilean local elections.

text.p: Parties in President Eduardo Frei's center-left coalition won Chile's municipal elections by a wide margin on Sunday, but an alliance of two rightist parties made significant gains, early results showed.

With 10 percent of the vote counted, the four parties in the governing coalition known as La Concertacion scored 53 percent of the vote, compared to 37 percent for the two-party rightist alliance known as the Union for Chile, official figures showed.
The results were announced on live television by Deputy Interior Secretary Belisario Velasco.

Frei's Christian Democratic Party alone won 24 percent -- below expectations, and down sharply from the 29 percent it won in Chie's last municipal elections in 1992, but its three coalition partners all raised their shares.
